Loss of protein function resulting in severe phenotypes of X-linked myotubular myopathy caused by novel synonymous and splice-site variants in the MTM1 gene. X-linked myotubular myopathy (XLMTM) is a severe, often neonatally lethal congenital neuromuscular disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the MTM1 gene. Affected neonates typically present with profound hypotonia, generalized muscle weakness, and respiratory insufficiency requiring immediate ventilatory support at birth. Splice-site variants in MTM1 account for approximately 20% of molecularly confirmed cases of XLMTM.
